observed_nexus_usage: ORDER sec.24 D_LAYER: declared non-collapse relation between two semantic types/states
repo E0.2 gate code: state value returned for missing/unknown input (S.AIR_GAP); unknown strings default to AIR_GAP; integrated GATE5 returns AIR_GAP where standalone returns FALSIFIED (L3-053)
pairs.SOURCE_FORMAL_DESCRIPTION: Two variants that must be disambiguated. (A) Relation sense: for declared types/states X and Y, the invariant NOT(collapse(X,Y)) holds — no operation may map an X-object to a Y-object without an explicit, logged, authorized transition. (B) State sense: gate output UNRESOLVED, emitted when a required input is absent or unparseable; UNRESOLVED blocks promotion and is distinct from FALSIFIED (evidence contradicts) and VERIFIED.
pairs.METAPHOR: An air gap: an open space between two things that must not silently close.

maps: the two sides of the gap
two declared semantic types or states (sense A) / evidence-present vs evidence-absent (sense B)
an undeclared conversion or inference across the boundary
the system must keep reporting UNRESOLVED rather than defaulting to VERIFIED or FALSIFIED
DECODE_KEY.required_sense_tag: Every use MUST state AIR_GAP[RELATION] or AIR_GAP[STATE]

INFORMATION_LOST: which of the two senses is meant
the difference between UNRESOLVED and FALSIFIED (code shows two implementations disagree)
pairs.MISLEADING_INFERENCE_RISK: HIGH. Dominant technical meaning (NIST/CNSSI/RFC 4949: systems not physically connected, transfer only manual under human control; L3-049) invites the false inference that NEXUS nodes are network-isolated or that a security boundary exists. Internal polysemy (relation vs state) already produced divergent gate behaviour.
pairs.SAFE_USE_CONTEXT: Internal design discussion where the sense tag and the formal predicate are printed alongside.
PROHIBITED_USE_CONTEXT: as an enum/state name in executable code without a mapping table
as evidence that a boundary is enforced
pairs.leak_test: Rename AIR_GAP->UNRESOLVED in code and AIR GAP->NON_COLLAPSE_RELATION in text; predictions/gates/fixtures must be unchanged. Current status: rename is behaviour-neutral in code, but the textual D_LAYER does not match code semantics -> DECODE_INCONSISTENCY (fix before use).

pairs.SOURCE_FORMAL_DESCRIPTION: Proposed decode (lane-3 reconstruction from ORDER sec. 5, 9): nodes N_1..N_k share a governance rule set C (D_CONTROL overlap high) while their epistemic inputs (source, data, method, model = D_EPISTEMIC) are independent or bounded-dependent; desired properties: warranted convergence, justified dissent retention, minority-correct retention, error decorrelation, calibration, revision accuracy. Also invites biological descent and authority-by-descent readings. The positive word hides the negative constraint that is the actual hypothesis.

PROHIBITED_USE_CONTEXT: as a claim that nodes are independent

pairs.SOURCE_FORMAL_DESCRIPTION: (A) Receipt sense: a record R = {sender_id, receiver_id, object_sha256, byte_length, timestamp, status} by which a receiver attests it holds bytes with a given digest. (B) Protocol sense: an interactive challenge-response establishing capability or key possession before exchange. Neither establishes truth, authority, or identity without a trust root.
pairs.METAPHOR: A handshake: two parties greet and agree.

maps: receipt of identical bytes (A) or completed challenge (B)
does_not_map: mutual authentication unless keys and a trust root are bound

INFORMATION_LOST: that agreement is about bytes, not meaning
pairs.MISLEADING_INFERENCE_RISK: MEDIUM-HIGH. Network-protocol meaning (TLS 1.3 handshake authenticates parties and negotiates cryptographic parameters; L3-056) implies an authenticated exchange; social meaning implies consensus. NEXUS receipts are neither by default.
pairs.SAFE_USE_CONTEXT: File-name label for byte-acknowledgement receipts with a schema.
PROHIBITED_USE_CONTEXT: describing an unimplemented online protocol as established
pairs.leak_test: Rename to BYTE_RECEIPT (A) or CAPABILITY_CHALLENGE (B); schema validators unchanged.
